title: Relies on your own willpower. No science behind it.
body:
An absolute barrage of impossible-to-follow psychobabble filled with ads for liver cleansing products. Nothing intuitive or helpful about it.

Firstly, the number of "ad-ons" we are prompted to buy is overwhelming. Secondly, I didn't appreciate the insidious nature of the messages we had to click in order to say, "no thanks". What I mean by that is that every time you click that you don't want the $59 milk thistle or whatever liver concoction you're selling (by the way, clinical trials of milk thistle have produced very mixed results. There is ZERO conclusive evidence it helps your liver at all), the "no thanks" button is actually a "no I do not wish to improve my health" (or wording to that effect) button.

Then there is the app and Optimal Routine PDF. All of it relies on self-entering data based on the will power and initiative of the very person who has shown no will power to stop drinking. There is not a scintilla of evidence-based or scientific approach to reforming the behaviour of someone who would like to reduce their drinking. 

You could literally grab an A4 piece of paper, draw up a table and tally up how many times you've "hydrated", "socialized" or "engaged in deep breathing". Those things (socializing, deep breathing, sleeping, water) do work, but the app does nothing to actually help you modify your habits. It's essentially an app that says, "hey, you should change your habits". I'd rather pay my wife that money to tell me that, while I get a little crayon and mark it on the wall.

body:

But to my surprise, I was still charged around €50, which is not normal because they are only supposed to take the card details and charge you only if the trial continues.

The following month, I noticed a withdrawal of about €75, even though after checking I had no active subscription on the app. I hadn’t even used it once anyway, because it’s completely useless. So I basically got ROBBED of more than €100 by this app. I want to stress that at NO point did I agree to pay for anything.

Of course, during this time I sent them about 4 emails demanding a refund, but of course they never replied. In short, don’t download this app, it’s just an AI created to steal money from people during sign-up, and they even keep your card afterwards to keep charging you (by the way, the €75 was taken with no invoice and no explanation at all).
